Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. Title: Diagnosis of test `testIssue695`

Details:
The test `testIssue695` defines a simple first-order differential equation with a derivative always equal to 1.0 and integrates it from 0.0 to 30.0 time units using the DormandPrince853Integrator. Two event handlers of type `ResettingEvent` are registered at times 10.99 and 11.01 with very small tolerance and maximum check counts. The initial step size is set to 3.0.

The key point lies in the `ResettingEvent` class, which contains a method `g(double t, double[] y)` that includes an assertion:

```java
Assert.assertTrue("going backard in time! (" + t + " < " + lastTriggerTime + ")", t >= lastTriggerTime);
return t - tEvent;
```

This assertion checks that the `g` function is never called at a time `t` less than the last event trigger time `lastTriggerTime`. The exception thrown by this assertion implies the integrator or event handling machinery is calling the event function at obsolete (earlier) times, which violates the expected behavior of no backward time calls after event triggers.

The test failure thus results from the event handling mechanism allowing a backward evaluation of the event detection function `g` despite an event having already been triggered and time having moved forward. This is consistent with the commented explanation above the assertion regarding issue 695:

```java
// the bug corresponding to issue 695 causes the g function
// to be called at obsolete times t despite an event
// occurring later has already been triggered.
```

Therefore, the root cause of the test failure is that the event detector in the integrator is not properly managing event times after an event has been triggered, resulting in calls to `g` at previous times less than `lastTriggerTime`.

Suggested places to inspect and fix would be in the event detection and event state management logic within the ODE integrator and event handler related classes.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.math.ode.events.ResettingEvent.g(double,double[])
org.apache.commons.math.ode.events.EventState.checkAndUpdate(double)  (likely, to prevent backward calls)
org.apache.commons.math.ode.events.EventState.tryAdvance(double)  (likely, event time progression logic)
org.apache.commons.math.ode.nonstiff.DormandPrince853Integrator.integrate(...)  (integration step and event handling coordination)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
